searchText: hey all I'm trying to dig into the execution specs repo, and wanted to ask a couple of very beginner-level questions here, if someone has the time and is interested in answering * let's say I wanted to build a client - how would I use the specs to know what/how to build? * I think another way of asking this is how can I read the spec, using the repo? * how would I test the client using the specs? is that too language-dependent to answer? just to be very clear from the beginning, I have an interest potentially recreating something like the execution specs for a different EVM chain You may have better luck over in <#856943705209569291>. cc <@689161464829050960> Hm, I guess the easiest would be to straight up port the Python into whatever language you want your client to be written in. You'd end up with a working, but poorly performing, client. A slightly more useful way to do it would be to go through the EIPs for each fork, read 'em, and use EELS as a reference to figure out what the EIPs want you to implement. EELS? ethereum execution layer specification 😛 the execution-specs repo

excerpts.author: wschwab
excerpts.content:
hey all

I'm trying to dig into the execution specs repo, and wanted to ask a couple of very beginner-level questions here, if someone has the time and is interested in answering

* let's say I wanted to build a client - how would I use the specs to know what/how to build?
    * I think another way of asking this is how can I read the spec, using the repo?
* how would I test the client using the specs? is that too language-dependent to answer?

just to be very clear from the beginning, I have an interest potentially recreating something like the execution specs for a different EVM chain

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: Hm, I guess the easiest would be to straight up port the Python into whatever language you want your client to be written in. You'd end up with a working, but poorly performing, client.
